title: Huxley-Gödel Machine: Human-Level Coding Agent Development by an Approximation of the Optimal Self-Improving Machine
summary: HGM guides self-improving coding agent search with clade-level metaproductivity (CMP) estimates instead of benchmark scores, provably approximating the Gödel Machine and achieving human-level coding agent design on SWE-bench Lite.

title: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
summary: A fixed LLM iteratively improves its own agent harness via weakness mining, bounded edit proposals, and regression-gated validation, lifting held-out Terminal-Bench-2.0 pass rates by up to 21.4 points across three model families.

title: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
summary: Harness-updating is flat across model capability tiers while harness-benefit is non-monotonic — mid-tier models gain most, weak models fail at harness activation and adherence.

title: Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses
summary: AHE is an observability-driven closed loop that auto-evolves a coding agent's harness (prompt/tools/middleware/memory) by binding every file-level edit to a falsifiable manifest, lifting Terminal-Bench 2 pass@1 from 69.7% to 77.0% in 10 iterations and transferring zero-shot to SWE-bench and four alternate base-model families.

title: AutoHarness: improving LLM agents by automatically synthesizing a code harness
summary: AutoHarness uses LLM-driven iterative code refinement with Thompson sampling tree search to automatically synthesize code harnesses that eliminate illegal moves in 145 TextArena games, enabling smaller models to outperform larger ones.

title: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses
summary: An outer-loop system that uses a coding agent with full filesystem access to prior code, traces, and scores to automatically search over LLM harness code, outperforming hand-designed harnesses on text classification (+7.7pp), math reasoning (+4.7pp), and agentic coding tasks.

title: A Subgoal-driven Framework for Improving Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: MiRA unifies subgoal-based inference-time planning with potential-based RL reward shaping to boost Gemma3-12B from 6.4% to 43.0% success rate on WebArena-Lite, surpassing proprietary models and prior open-source SOTA.

title: Learning to Discover at Test Time
summary: TTT-Discover performs reinforcement learning at test time with an entropic objective and PUCT-based state reuse, enabling LLMs to continuously improve on individual scientific problems and achieving new state-of-the-art across mathematics, GPU kernel engineering, algorithm design, and biology.

title: MetaClaw: Just Talk - An Agent That Meta-Learns and Evolves in the Wild
summary: A continual meta-learning framework that enables deployed LLM agents to evolve through dual-timescale adaptation: gradient-free skill injection from failures and opportunistic RL-based policy optimization during idle windows.

title: On-Policy Context Distillation for Language Models
summary: OPCD trains a student model on its own generated trajectories while minimizing reverse KL divergence against a context-conditioned teacher, enabling robust internalization of transient in-context knowledge (experiential knowledge and system prompts) into model parameters.

title: Aligning Language Models from User Interactions
summary: SDPO learns directly from multi-turn user interactions via self-distillation — using the user's follow-up message as hindsight context to derive token-level advantages — improving alignment benchmarks on Qwen3/Olmo3 without explicit rewards or preference labels.

title: Reinforcing Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Self-Evolving Rubrics
summary: RLCER enables a single LLM to self-propose and self-evolve rubrics for direct CoT supervision during RLVR training, outperforming outcome-centric RLVR without any human annotation.

title: OpenClaw-RL: Train Any Agent Simply by Talking
summary: OpenClaw-RL recovers evaluative and directive signals from live next-state interactions to train any agent continuously via Binary RL and Hindsight-Guided On-Policy Distillation, achieving a 4.8x gain on personal agent personalization and consistent improvements across terminal, GUI, SWE, and tool-call settings.

title: SKILLRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
summary: SKILLRL distills raw trajectories into a hierarchical skill library (SKILLBANK) and co-evolves that library with the agent's RL policy through recursive failure analysis.
